REWARD_MACHINE:
STATES: u0, u1, u2
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u2
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, at_exit & holding_box) -> u2
(u0, box_fell) -> u1
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, at_exit & holding_box) -> u2
(u1, holding_box & !at_exit) -> u0
(u1, !holding_box) -> u0
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, else) -> u2
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, at_exit & holding_box, u2) -> 1.0
(u1, at_exit & holding_box, u2) -> 1.0
(u1, holding_box & !at_exit, u0) -> 0.1
feedback:
Accept. Format: all required headers present; FINAL_STATES is nonempty, its single state u2 is declared in STATES and is the accepting goal state reached exactly on task success. Guards use only the five given propositions with Boolean connectives (predicate-only), and reward entries correspond one-to-one to declared transitions with identical guards.

Semantic fidelity: the success edge (u0, at_exit & holding_box) -> u2 with reward 1.0 matches the setup's exit condition (box in hands); stepping onto the exit without the box falls through u0's else self-loop and yields 0, matching the environment's 0 payment. Event/persistent distinction is correct: box_fell is used only as a one-step edge trigger (u0 -> u1), never as a persistent condition, while holding_box drives the return and goal guards.

Irrelevant-event coverage: siren_ringing and switch_toggled appear in no guard. u0's else self-loop absorbs them; from u1 the three explicit guards are mutually exclusive and exhaustive (their union is every assignment), so co-occurring siren starts or toggles cannot derail tracking — the step is routed by holding_box status alone, which is the right behavior since the task does not involve the siren. u1's else is therefore vacuous; harmless.

Ordered coverage: all realizable event orders are handled — fall -> immediate pickup -> second fall -> immediate pickup -> exit (u0->u1->u0->u1->u0->u2), fall with a missed pickup (u1 -> u0 via !holding_box), and a drop-then-repickup-on-the-due-step corner case where the fall fires the same step: the RM is in u0 then (the drop went through u0's else), so (u0, box_fell) -> u1 arms the next-step 0.1 correctly.

Reward safety: the 0.1 fires only for pickup on the step right after a fall, exactly matching 'very next move' (in the face world the fall turns the agent toward the box, so it is always achievable). At most two falls occur per episode, bounding shaping at 0.2 < 1.0. Deliberate drop/pickup cycles cannot farm it: a drop from u0 goes through else and stays in u0, so no new 0.1 is armed without a genuine exogenous fall. Missing the immediate pickup costs only the bonus, never the terminal 1.0, so the RM never blocks task completion. No reward is obtainable off-task.

Reachability: u1 (first fall always occurs) and u2 are reachable. Two dead entries exist and are non-blocking: (u1, at_exit & holding_box) -> u2 with its 1.0 entry is unreachable — box_fell and at_exit never co-occur, and from u1 one action cannot both pick the box up and step onto the exit, while u1 is exited every step — and (u1, else) never fires since the explicit guards already cover all assignments. They are consistent with the machine's semantics and cannot fire spuriously; noted as a minor compactness redundancy only.
